messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service=dedicated-inference, tenant=VelvetHealth, cluster=dv-velvet-01, symptom=high_p95_latency + increased_5xx_count :rotating_light:
pagerduty: INC123456 triggered by policy 'dedicated-tenant-latency' — page sent to #eng-oncall and on-call rotation
alice (oncall): Acked INC123456 — I'm on it. Starting triage. Seeing page, grabbing latest dashboards.
bhavik (sre): I can help — will check KV cache metrics and queue depth. Any immediate customer impact?
carla (solutions): Customer CS reported a spike in 503s for their webhooks ~2m ago. They've flagged degraded UX. They're on standby for updates.
mike (infra): Noted. I can try to open burst capacity if autoscaler isn't responding. Where's traffic routed?
alice (oncall): Current routing: dv-velvet-01 primary in us-east-1, replica in us-west-2. Traffic still hitting primary. Dashboards show p95 generation latency up from 300ms -> 1.8s and 5xx rate ~2.4% (normally <0.1%). Queue length for tenant_queue_velvet up ~850 -> 3200.
bhavik (sre): Pulling logs from dv-velvet-01 now. Suspect KV cache thrash or model-serving slowdown.
carla (solutions): Customer says this impacts checkout flow, high severity for them. They want ETA.
alice (oncall): Short-term plan: 1) route a % of VelvetHealth traffic to us-west-2 replica; 2) enable soft-throttle for non-critical endpoints; 3) if needed, fallback Velvet to smaller model variant (gptx-small-q4) for the next 10m to reduce latency. Does that align?
bhavik (sre): Agree. I'll check whether the us-west replica has warmed KV cache for Velvet model. If not, fallback to smaller model might be fastest.
mike (infra): Preparing burst request to reserved pool — sending now. Command: 
```
rbctl capacity burst --cluster dv-velvet-01 --units 4 --reason "INC123456 latency mitigation"
```
(Waiting on approval from billing guard)
velvet-alert-bot: Notified customer contact: velvet-sre@velvethealth.com — message queued.
carla (solutions): I'll let them know we're routing traffic and may switch to a smaller variant temporarily. Keep me posted for a customer-facing ETA.
alice (oncall): Executing traffic-split to us-west-2 replica 10% now. Command: 
```
routes set-split --tenant VelvetHealth --from dv-velvet-01 --to dv-velvet-02 --percent 10
```
...10% rollout complete. Monitoring latency impact.
bhavik (sre): KV cache miss rate spiked to 82% on primary; replica miss rate 7% (already warm thanks to background prewarm). The 10% split dropped p95 for that fraction to ~420ms. Good sign.
alice (oncall): Increasing split to 40% while we watch errors. Doing 40% now.
...40% split applied. Overall p95 down from 1.8s -> 1.1s, 5xx down from 2.4% -> 1.1%. Queue decreasing.
mike (infra): Burst request approved by billing guard, units provisioned. Should help throughput if we need more.
bhavik (sre): Recommend also enabling per-tenant soft-throttle for expensive ops (long generations) to keep latency SLOs. Command to enable: 
```
rbctl tenant-config set VelvetHealth --soft-throttle true --threshold-ms 1200
```
alice (oncall): Enabling soft-throttle. Note: this will slow some long requests and return 429s for low-priority work.
velvet-alert-bot: Customer acknowledged initial note and asked for ETA ~15m.
carla (solutions): Telling customer 15-30m while we stabilize with routing + throttle.
bhavik (sre): Logs show a GC stall on one of the model workers and CPU steal on pod velv-serve-07. Looking at pod metrics: 92% CPU, swap-backed memory pressure. Possible kernel OOM risk.
mike (infra): I'm evacuating velv-serve-07 and draining. Command: 
```
kubectl drain velv-serve-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
(Draining)
...pod drained. New replica spun up from node pool with available resources. New pod joined cluster.
alice (oncall): Good. After draining, p95 improved further to ~850ms overall, 5xx ~0.7%. Queue continuing to fall.
bhavik (sre): For safety, switching VelvetHealth to fallback model variant (gptx-small-q4) for 15m window to prevent recurrence while we analyze root cause. Command: 
```
models set-fallback --tenant VelvetHealth --from gptx-medium --to gptx-small-q4 --duration 15m --reason "INC123456 mitigation"
```
...fallback applied. Observed p95 ~420ms, 5xx ~0.15%. Customer reported improvement.
carla (solutions): Customer confirms their checkout flow is back to normal. They thanked us. Marking customer impact reduced.
alice (oncall): Creating PD incident note and assigning to SRE for postmortem. Also will notify postmortem board.
pagerduty: Incident INC123456 acknowledged by alice (oncall) and assigned to bhavik (sre) for follow-up.
bhavik (sre): I'll keep the incident open and collect heap/dump/artifacts. Initial hypothesis: worker memory leak + node contention causing GC spikes -> KV cache thrash -> long-tail latency. Will instrument VMs and check kernel logs.
carla (solutions): Please also track customer-facing timeline and the exact minutes when we routed traffic, drained pod, and applied fallback. I'll prepare a summary for the customer.
alice (oncall): Timeline so far recorded in PD notes. Next steps: bhavik to own root-cause, mike to audit node pool for any similar pressure, carla to own customer comms. I'll hand this to night on-call in 45m.
velvet-alert-bot: Customer Slack webhook notified: status=stabilized; further updates to follow.
alice (oncall): Handoff plan: leave the incident in monitoring, rollback fallback only when p95 < 600ms for 10m and no uptick in 5xx. Night on-call (maya) please be ready to escalate if metrics regress.
maya (oncall-next): Acknowledged — I'll monitor the dashboards and take over if needed.
bhavik (sre): Dumping additional logs to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/INC123456/artifacts/ — collecting gc logs, kernel logs, pod logs.
alice (oncall): Thanks team. I'll close the immediate page once PD incident is marked stable. Leaving open for postmortem follow-up. :white_check_mark:
